record.title: WaveletECO reports a specialized local model matching a frontier API on chip-repair scores at lower estimated inference cost
record.summary: The authors combine a closed-loop engineering-change-order workflow with a Qwen3.5-9B model trained on repair demonstrations and action preferences. Across 22 chip designs and 594 runs, they report a mean repair score of 79.65 for INT8 and 79.63 for BF16, versus 77.44 for GPT-6 Astra under a shared execution protocol. Their cost model estimates INT8 inference at $0.00226 per task versus $0.33188 for GPT-6 Astra, about 1/147 as much, excluding EDA and idle costs. These are author-reported results from one benchmark; nine designs are held out, but the broader generalization and deployment economics remain unverified.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across 22 designs and three repeats per model-design pair, the authors report WaveletECO-Policy INT8 and BF16 repair scores of 79.65 and 79.63, respectively, compared with 77.44 for GPT-6 Astra under the same execution protocol and a 1% area-growth limit.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors estimate INT8 inference at $0.00226 per task and GPT-6 Astra at $0.33188 per task, or about 1/147 the cost, based on measured local throughput and dated API and GPU-rental prices; the estimate excludes EDA and idle costs.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish that the cost ratio or score advantage transfers to different EDA backends, larger design populations, other technology nodes or end-to-end production costs; the deployments used for cost estimation were not re-evaluated for repair quality.

evidence_gaps.description: Repair-quality and cost claims have not been independently reproduced; the cost model is limited to inference and specified September 2026 prices/rental proxies.
Benchmark uses 22 designs from one setting and one EDA backend; transfer across nodes, design types and toolchains is unmeasured.

brief.importance_rationale: If the benchmark and inference-cost results generalize, specialized local models could alter the cost and provider-dependence trade-off for physical chip repair workflows. Score 6 reflects potential importance to a high-cost engineering domain, not truth or transfer beyond the tested designs.
limitations: All experimental findings and costs are author-reported; the research desk did not reproduce the benchmark or cost model.
The benchmark has 22 designs, nine held out; the paper does not establish transfer to larger or more diverse designs and technology nodes.
The shared execution interface uses one EDA backend, one candidate repair action per round and a 1% area-growth limit.

The 1/147 ratio is estimated inference cost only. It uses fixed API prices and GPU-rental/throughput estimates and excludes EDA and idle costs; the cost-estimation deployments were not re-evaluated for repair quality.
brief.summary: The authors combine a closed-loop engineering-change-order workflow with a Qwen3.5-9B model trained on repair demonstrations and action preferences. Across 22 chip designs and 594 runs, they report a mean repair score of 79.65 for INT8 and 79.63 for BF16, versus 77.44 for GPT-6 Astra under a shared execution protocol. Their cost model estimates INT8 inference at $0.00226 per task versus $0.33188 for GPT-6 Astra, about 1/147 as much, excluding EDA and idle costs. These are author-reported results from one benchmark; nine designs are held out, but the broader generalization and deployment economics remain unverified.

technical.claimed_result: In 594 runs over 22 designs (three repeats for each of nine model variants per design), WaveletECO-Policy INT8 scores 79.65 and BF16 79.63, versus GPT-6 Astra 77.44 under the shared protocol. INT8 estimated inference cost is $0.00226/task versus $0.33188/task for GPT-6 Astra, a modeled 146.8× score-per-dollar comparison.
technical.compute_or_cost: Authors estimate $0.00226 per task for INT8 versus $0.33188 for GPT-6 Astra, about 1/147 as much; estimate excludes EDA and idle costs and depends on the specified throughput and GPU/API prices. No total production-cost estimate is given.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected paper documents the workflow, benchmark protocol, score definition, author-reported measurements and cost model. Neither performance nor cost was independently reproduced in this activation.
technical.implementation_status: Paper describes an evaluated closed-loop platform and locally deployed 9B model; no independent deployment or external EDA integration was verified in this activation.
technical.mechanism: A shared physical ECO workflow reads timing, electrical and library state, selects a repair action, executes and measures it, then retains accepted changes or rolls back rejected ones. A local Qwen3.5-9B model is trained with supervised fine-tuning and CPO-SimPO preference data from same-state repair actions; quantized variants use INT8 or INT4 weights with BF16 activations.
technical.regime: 22 physical chip designs, 13 used for adaptation/model selection and nine held out; up to five repair rounds; three repeats per model/design; one candidate action per round and 1% area-growth limit. Local inference-cost estimates use single GPUs (BF16 on RTX 6000D, INT8/INT4 on RTX 4090); API reference prices were recorded September 19, 2026.
technical.reproducibility: Paper provides a defined score, shared execution rules, 22-design split and three repeats. Independent reproduction and transfer to new toolchains/designs remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: GPT-6 Astra scored 77.44 under the same ECO execution interface across the same design set. The authors also compare local Qwen3.5-9B direct and thinking variants, WaveletECO SFT, GPT-5.6 Sol and DeepSeek V4. The quality score and cost estimate are not a matched deployment comparison because cost-estimation deployments were not re-evaluated for repair quality.

brief.title: WaveletECO reports a specialized local model matching a frontier API on chip-repair scores at lower estimated inference cost
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported quality and cost estimates transfer to larger design sets and production workflows, a specialized local model could make multi-round physical chip repair cheaper while reducing dependence on paid frontier APIs. The reported cost ratio concerns inference only and uses estimated local GPU rental and throughput; it does not establish end-to-end EDA economics or a general advantage over frontier models.
